questions.qtext: Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) is a dimensionality reduction technique that

options.text: Maximize the variance in the original features.
Create new feature that are linear combinations of the original features.
Maximizes the separability between different class.

questions.solution:
(d)
LDA aims to maximize the distinction between different classes with in the data by deriving a linear combination of features. This facilitates effective separation between classes.

questions.qtext: What does the assumption of linearity in linear regression imply?

options.text: The relationship between the independent and dependent variables is non-linear.
The residuals exhibit a constant variance.
The relationship between the independent and dependent variables can be represented by a straight line.

questions.solution:
(c)
The assumption of linearity in linear regression implies that the relationship between the
independent and dependent variables can be captured by a straight-line model.
Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.qtext: In Ridge Regression, what does the penalty term added to the cost function in ridge regression penalize?
questions.solution:
(a)
In Ridge Regression, the penalty term (L2 regularization) penalizes large coefficients by adding the sum of squared coefficients to the cost function. This helps in preventing overfitting by shrinking the coefficients towards zero.

questions.qtext: In Lasso Regression, what does the penalty term added to the cost function encourage?
questions.solution:
(a)
In Lasso Regression, the penalty term (L1 regularization) encourages sparsity in the coefficients by adding the sum of absolute values of coefficients to the cost function. This leads to some coefficients being exactly zero, effectively performing feature selection.

questions.qtext:
Which of following statements is/are correct?
S1 : Linear support vector machine is a parametric algorithm.
S2 : KNN is a non-parametric algorithm.
questions.solution:
(c)
S1 : Linear support vector machine is a parametric because it can only produce linear boundaries.
So, S1 is true.
S2 : KNN is a non-parametric algorithm because it avoids a priori assumption about the shape of the class boundary and can thus adapt more closely to non-linear boundaries as the amount of training data increases.
So, S2 is true.

questions.qtext: How, can one address the bias-variance tradeoff in practice to enhance model performance?

options.text: By increasing the complexity of the model.
By decreasing the complexity of the model.
By using a more complex optimization algorithm.

questions.solution:
(b)
To address the bias-variance tradeoff, one can reduce model complexity by using simpler models, regularization techniques, or feature selection methods to prevent overfitting and improve generalization to unseen data.
